previous_description: Defines a callback where the API sends asynchronous notifications to an external URL derived at runtime. A callback maps a Runtime Expression (e.g., $request.body#/callbackUrl) to a full PathItem object, meaning the callback specifies the complete HTTP interaction — method, headers, and expected response — not just a target URL. Enables event-driven integrations and async workflows.
definition: An outbound HTTP request contract attached to an operation, in which the API itself calls a consumer-supplied URL. The URL is obtained by evaluating a runtime expression against the triggering request or response, and the full interaction (method, body, expected responses) is described as a PathItem.

distinguish_from.when: the HTTP interaction is one the API receives and serves on its own paths, rather than a request the API sends to a URL supplied by the consumer.
the relationship describes a follow-up call that the client makes to another operation of this API, using values from a response, rather than a call the API pushes to the client.
modelling the set of HTTP methods under a fixed path template of the API, or the inner PathItem that a callback aggregates, rather than the expression-keyed callback wrapper.
the target is a fixed or variable-templated deployment base URL of the API, not a URL resolved per request from a runtime expression.

code_evidence: A 'callbacks:' map under an operation in an OpenAPI YAML/JSON file whose keys are runtime expressions such as '{$request.body#/callbackUrl}'.
A route decorator or annotation declaring callbacks, such as FastAPI's callbacks= router parameter or springdoc/Swagger @Callback, on a subscription or job-submission endpoint.
Handler code that stores a callbackUrl/notifyUrl field from the incoming request and later issues an HTTP POST to it from a background job or event listener using an HTTP client.
notes: The callback's map-key name (e.g. 'onPaymentComplete') has no attribute, and it is unclear whether one node represents a named callback or a single expression entry. The 'uses api.server' relationship is dubious because callback targets are resolved at runtime. The layer description mentions webhooks, but no webhook type exists; webhooks are an OpenAPI 3.1 concept and could be confused with callbacks.
